environment.certified_pair_note: policyengine.py 6.20.2 pins and certifies policyengine-uk 2.177.7 with this file; the runs use policyengine-uk 2.179.1 (the author's instruction and the registered specification), so the model/data pair is not a certified one

checks: both probe calculations contain exactly two finite real non-Boolean monetary values and Boolean regulation flags per variable
both probe calculations have non-negative monetary values and Housing Benefit no greater than rent
the probe is under the pension-age Housing Benefit regulations
both probe benefit units are entitled to Guarantee Credit (guarantee_credit > 0)
Guarantee Credit entitlement is unchanged by claim and receipt overrides
only the claimant is paid Pension Credit
the claimant's Pension Credit includes its Guarantee Credit entitlement in both calculations
the entitled non-claimant's housing_benefit_assessable_capital is counted, not disregarded
the entitled non-claimant's housing_benefit_tariff_income is counted, not disregarded
the entitled non-claimant's housing_benefit_applicable_income is counted, not disregarded
the entitled non-claimant is not passported to maximum Housing Benefit
the claimant, in receipt of Guarantee Credit, is passported to maximum Housing Benefit
in_receipt_of_guarantee_credit set true passports the non-claimant
in_receipt_of_guarantee_credit set false means-tests the claimant

design.specification: docs/METHOD.md, 'Specification: full runs on a weighted sample of the Bayesian paths, 18 November 2026'

paths.not_identical_non_positive_rule: assigned to stratum 1 (the spec's strata cover positive-saving paths)

design.calendar_mapping: calendar growth in year t = central path's calendar growth + the path's statutory deviation from the centre in determination year t (September CPI, May-July earnings); 2039 takes the 2038 deviation. A zero-deviation path reproduces the central spec (max difference 0.0e+00).
design.stratification_variable: 2039-40 rule-arithmetic gross saving, £bn (b1_bayes.arithmetic, stored central run's base)

allocation.method: expected_value.allocate (Neyman on rule-arithmetic gross), min 4 per stratum

design.n_choice: N=100 (the registered minimum): the central rerun took 871 s at one worker on this shared host (about 40 GiB held by other workloads, ~14 GiB available); two workers give about 100 runs in ~12.5 h, finishing before 08:00 on 19 November

estimates.stratum_0: rules identical every April to 2039: net saving exactly zero (point mass W0); no household loses, so mean_loss_gbp is excluded from its median over paths (taken over positive-saving paths, weights W1..W10 renormalised)

mean_loss_gbp_weighted_median_over_paths.note: stratum 0 at the engine's 0 (no household loses); bootstrap seed 20261119

supplementary_ratio_estimator.method:
Not registered: a model-assisted check on the registered median. Full-run gross equals the rule arithmetic
(on the 6.20.2 central base) path by path, so each stratum's mean ratio of net (and of mean_loss_gbp) to gross,
applied to every one of the 399,440 paths' rule-arithmetic gross, gives a population median free of the
sampling noise in the 100-run median. Bootstrap: runs resampled within strata (2,000, seed fixed).

deviations: **Model version.** The registered text and the instruction name policyengine.py 6.20.2 with policyengine-uk 2.179.1, but 6.20.2's [uk] extra and bundle manifest pin and certify policyengine-uk 2.177.7 / core 3.34.10 with the fcfac709 Microcosm file. Installed: policyengine 6.20.2 (without [uk]), policyengine-uk 2.179.1, policyengine-core 3.34.10, and the file 6.20.2 certifies. The model/data pair is therefore uncertified (built and certified for 2.177.7).

**Host admission floor.** jobs.py's 40 GiB Microcosm reservation could not be met on this shared host (12-17 GiB available while other workloads held 25-45 GiB). Jobs were admitted against measured resident peaks (5.6-15 GiB; 6 GiB budget + 2 GiB + outstanding) with one or two workers, adjusted live; the runner was restarted once (19:16), discarding two in-progress jobs, which reran from scratch. None of this changes a result (the central rerun before and after reproduced bit for bit).

**Anchors in the queue.** The OBR long-term and central reruns ran in the sample queue (same specs and cache key as the anchors mode); the central path was run twice (before and after the path_following adaptation) with identical output.

**mean_loss_gbp over paths.** Its stratum-weighted median is taken over the positive-saving paths (strata 1-10, W renormalised): on stratum-0 paths no household loses and the engine reports 0. The 'median-gross stratum' is the stratum holding the all-path rule-arithmetic 2039 gross median (stratum 4, £8.1-10.1bn).

**Sample.** N = 100 draws as written to the design before any sample run (100 unique paths, no duplicate draws); all 100 completed, none failed after retry, so the failed-run min/max variants are not needed. The only failure (the first B1 path, model_new_state_pension 3.9e-4) predates the path_following adaptation and reran cleanly under it.
caveats: The registered median is the weighted median of 100 runs plus a point mass: a step function whose bootstrap intervals are asymmetric and whose value is set by a few runs in strata 3-5 (5-10 runs each). The supplementary ratio estimator (not registered) shows the size of that noise: £6.41bn against £6.70bn.

The stored-vs-rerun differences reflect model and data changes together (not decomposed): base 2039 flat-rate spending +0.27%; lower Pension Credit and Housing Benefit offsets on the wedge (PC 0.81 -> 0.76bn, HB 0.23 -> 0.15bn), consistent with 2.179.1 deriving the Savings Credit threshold and pension-age HB allowances from the earnings-linked guarantee (#2576; checked to match the model's own derivation) but also affected by the new dataset; a winter fuel offset near zero (0.027 -> 0.001bn); the State Pension age addition (#2340) present but identical under both rules. Anchor net/gross 0.675 -> 0.686 (wedge), 0.684 -> 0.686 (central).
Calendar CPI and earnings for each path are the central calendar path plus the path's statutory deviation (2039: the 2038 deviation), the registered modelling assumption.
Peak memory figures are resident set sizes; macOS compressed much of each job, whose footprint reached 10-14 GiB.
Run times are not representative of the model: median 636 s, up to 6,142 s, on a host thrashing under other workloads' memory load.
The weighted mean net is for the error budget only and is not for print.

adaptations.how: relaxed in memory by this script only: a DATASETS entry for the fcfac709 file (SHA-256 checked before every use by datasets.materialize) and check_upstream_2179, which admits exactly the 21 reviewed changed files of the 2.153.4 guard set and still fails if any other guarded file, or any of the builders the horizon extension and Scenario entry rely on (lagged series, statutory inputs, triple lock, private pension uprating, gov_balance, scenario, September-CPI uprating), differs

2.179.1 projects the model's own full new State Pension each April from the previous year's rate to the nearest 5p (create_rate_projection, not in 2.151.0). The unrounded expectation (tolerance 2e-4) failed on the first B1 path (3.9e-4). Expectation replaced by the same 5p-rounded rule on the model's own triple lock, checked exactly (1e-9); every other check unchanged

jobs.py reserves 40 GiB per Microcosm job; the shared host had 12-16 GiB available (about 40 GiB held, mostly compressed, by other workloads on the machine). Admission instead used host.assess with a floor of a 6 GiB job budget (resident peaks 5.6-15 GiB measured) + 2 GiB + what running jobs may still allocate; jobs ran partly compressed/swapped, which slows them but never changed a result

checks_outside_runs.linked_pension_credit_hb_derivation: On the 2.179.1 default parameter tree, Savings Credit threshold = guarantee - maximum/phase_in and pension-age HB aged = guarantee + maximum, aged_from_cutoff = guarantee, exactly in every projected year 2027-2039 (gaps only in published 2026: £0.04 and £0.003 a week), so set_flat_rates' linked branch reproduces the model's own derivation from the engine's earnings-linked guarantee.
checks_outside_runs.upstream_files_read: Diffs read against 2.153.4: the State Pension variables (basic, new, additional, state_pension input, state_pension_reported: age addition #2340 removed before the split, which the engine already handles), months_since_last_birthday (whole-population branch value only), create_economic_assumption_indices (horizon from the growth series; triple lock index unrounded), tax_benefit_system (new generation steps: State Pension 5p rate projection, linked PC/HB projection, UK total growth, energy indices), utils.parameters (fiscal-year conversion keeps 2015-2041 annual records), gov_tax/gov_spending (adds LISA charges/bonus, household_energy_payment, wales_childcare_offer: picked up by fiscal_variables, which reads the lists), create_earnings_uprating (docstring only), simulation.py against 2.177.7 (stored-draw input checks, dataset identifier checks). Admitted on run-time checks without a line-by-line read: the full 2.153.4->2.179.1 simulation.py diff and the two PC/HB builders (behaviour checked above) and the six PC/HB YAMLs.
checks_outside_runs.guard_set_note: The 2.153.4 guard set used here omits household_tax and household_benefits, which 2.151.0's guards include and which differ on 2.179.1; the engine's run-time government/household income identity (totals, saving_components) covers them on every run.
